posts.headline: Five editions running I've hammered One Nut Barner and Put it in Ra still hasn't said a word back — that's what a 20-8, back-to-back top-2, zero-ring resume does to a man on draft night.
posts.detail: 20-8 career record and a 1.5 average finish is Cowboys-level hype, but until there's a banner, silence is just pressure with no answer.

posts.headline: Sasinci's World walks into the draft room with a title on the mantle and a losing 13-15 record following him like a shadow — put up or shut up, Big Head.
posts.detail: One ring in two seasons doesn't erase a 5.5 average finish; Milk Man needs this draft to prove the banner wasn't a fluke.5

posts.headline: talentedtenthh has gone six straight editions without a peep, and draft night is the last chance for Chauncey to prove the 4-10, dead-last-12 season was a fluke and not a preview.
posts.detail: A 0.286 win pct and worst-in-league 12th place finish don't get fixed by staying quiet — they get baked in as identity.

posts.kicker: BIBLE OR THE BELT: JUDGMENT DAY
posts.headline: Draft night is Eli's Judgment Day — pick the Bible or pick the Belt, because 13-14-1 and a 5.5 average finish is purgatory, and purgatory doesn't draft championships.
posts.detail: The Ultimate Light Skin has had two seasons to choose a philosophy and instead delivered scripture-less mediocrity — time to bring fire and brimstone or go home.

posts.headline: The Thicks finally has a ring to defend this draft, but a modest 14-14 career mark means #FreeMaxx Champions is one bad draft board away from proving the title was a mirage.
posts.detail: A 5.5 average finish across two seasons is no dynasty resume — Tyrique14 needs to draft like a champion, not a .500 team that got hot once.
